patches.old: **Leon Festinger** and later **David Funder** developed the concept of **situational strength** to explain when traits predict behavior and when they do not.
patches.new: The concept of **situational strength** — developed by **Walter Mischel** himself in the 1970s and extended in later work by **Snyder and Ickes** and by industrial-organisational researchers — explains when traits predict behaviour and when they do not.

sources.title: OpenStax, Psychology §11.7 — trait theorists, covering the five factor model and the trait tradition the debate concerns

visual.title: How the debate went, and what settled it
visual.alt: A four-step sequence from trait theory's promise through Mischel's 0.30 correlations and Epstein's aggregation argument to interactionism; a contrast of strong and weak situations with the kinds of setting each describes and the effect on trait prediction; three if-then rows showing the same child behaving differently by context while the pattern stays fixed; and a comparison of projective and objective tests with what each trades away.
visual.caption: One observation is one test item. Average fourteen days of behaviour and the same correlations climb from 0.3 to 0.8 — the traits were there, the measurement was not.
